title: Just look at him (Teresa, Way of Perfection 26)
hook: I'm not asking you to think much, only to look at him
tomorrow: what fits on a bookmark and holds up a whole life?

segments.voice: Yesterday Teresa called prayer a close sharing between friends. Yesterday's line: time with a friend.

Ten minutes set aside to pray, and the mind is already at the group chat, the unpaid bill, the thing somebody said at lunch. Push harder for holy thoughts and they slip away faster. Teresa knew that kind of prayer time. Writing to the sisters of her convent in The Way of Perfection, she does something kind: she lowers the bar almost to the floor.
screen: `TEN MINUTES, MIND ELSEWHERE.` → `TERESA LOWERS THE BAR.` → `ALMOST TO THE FLOOR.`

segments.voice: Here's the heart of it, in the sense of chapter twenty-six: I'm not asking you to think much about him, or come up with many ideas, or make long, clever meditations. I'm only asking you to look at him. Not analyze. Look. And she asks: who could stop you turning the eyes of your soul toward him, even for a moment? Then she makes it personal. Meet him where you are. If you're glad, look at him risen. If you're struggling or sad, look at him on the way to the garden, or carrying the cross. Whatever the mood, there's a scene that fits it. Then the part that turns it around: he is already looking at you. You aren't trying to catch his attention; you're returning a gaze. The letter to the Hebrews comes close: "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith." Teresa's version is gentler. Not a test of concentration. A glance, and then another, every time the mind wanders off and comes back. In her picture, the wandering isn't the failure. It's the moment to look again.
screen: `NOT THINK MUCH. JUST LOOK.` · `A SCENE FOR EVERY MOOD.` · `HE'S ALREADY LOOKING.` · `A GLANCE, THEN ANOTHER.` · then, large: `JUST LOOK AT HIM.`

segments.voice: If there's an image of Christ near you, a cross, an icon, a painting on your phone, rest your eyes on it. Don't think about it; just look, and when your mind wanders, come back to looking. If that image isn't yours, look at one thing in front of you with the same quiet attention.
Just look at him. Teresa's prayer for wandering minds: not more thoughts, only a glance toward him.
Keep this one: just look at him, and look again whenever the mind wanders. Day sixteen fifty.

screen: `DAY 1650 COUNTS.` → `THE SAINTS IN THEIR OWN WORDS · 49 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT FITS ON A BOOKMARK AND HOLDS UP A WHOLE LIFE?`
